dashboard.label: Escalation rules
dashboard.description: Site rules that lift a finding above what the score alone would give it: what each would move, and the switch to turn it on.

div.b: Every rule ships switched off, and this page is where you decide whether to switch one on.
div.span: An escalation rule re-orders the queue for the whole estate. It never invents a finding, never changes a CVE's severity and never lowers anything: a rule can only bump a finding up. The replay below runs every rule against the fleet as it stands right now and reports what would move, without moving anything. Read it before you touch a switch.

A switch here changes the rule's enabled flag and recompiles the macro the evaluation search expands, both through Splunk's own configuration service, so on a search head cluster every member sees the same rule set. Conditions and bumps are not edited here on purpose: a predicate applied to every finding in the estate is a change somebody should review as a diff, in riskability_escalations.conf.

panel.title: What each rule would move, replayed against the fleet now

search.query: | savedsearch "Riskability - replay escalation rules" | eval Move = from_tier . " to " . to_tier | rename rule AS Rule, enabled AS "On", findings AS Findings, hosts AS Hosts, cves AS CVEs | table Rule, "On", Move, Findings, Hosts, CVEs

div.span: A rule that would move thousands of findings is not thereby a good rule: it is a rule that has stopped discriminating, and a queue where everything is urgent is a queue with no order in it. The useful shape is a small number of findings moved for a reason you can state in one sentence.
